name: Solving linear equations
prerequisites: Be able to add, subtract, multiply and divide signed numbers.
Be able to simplify like terms and expand a bracket.
Be able to use inverse operations to undo a calculation.
learningOutcomes: Can you isolate the unknown by performing the same operation on both sides?
Can you solve a linear equation containing brackets or fractions?
Can you substitute your answer into the original equation to check it?

name: Linear functions
prerequisites: Be able to plot an ordered pair on Cartesian axes.
Be able to substitute a number into an algebraic expression.
Be able to calculate a change in y divided by a change in x.
learningOutcomes: Can you draw the graph of y = mx + c from its equation?
Can you identify the gradient and the x- and y-intercepts?
Can you determine the equation of a straight line from given information?

name: Quadratic functions
prerequisites: Be able to square signed numbers and substitute them into an expression.
Be able to plot ordered pairs on Cartesian axes.
Be able to factor a simple quadratic expression.
Be able to solve an equation by setting each factor equal to zero.
learningOutcomes: Can you sketch a quadratic graph and label its intercepts?
Can you identify its turning point, axis of symmetry and direction of opening?
Can you describe how changing the parameters changes the graph?

name: Exponential functions
prerequisites: Be able to evaluate positive and negative integer powers.
Be able to substitute a value into an expression.
Be able to plot ordered pairs on Cartesian axes.
learningOutcomes: Can you draw an exponential graph from a table of values?
Can you identify its intercepts and horizontal asymptote?
Can you distinguish exponential growth from exponential decay?

name: Sine rule
prerequisites: Be able to match each side of a triangle to its opposite angle.
Be able to use the angle sum of a triangle to find a missing angle.
Be able to calculate sine and inverse sine in degree mode.
Be able to rearrange a proportion to make an unknown the subject.
learningOutcomes: Can you identify when the sine rule can be used?
Can you find a missing side using a known opposite side-angle pair?
Can you find a missing angle and check whether another valid triangle is possible?

name: Cosine rule
prerequisites: Be able to identify the angle between two given sides of a triangle.
Be able to square a number and calculate its square root.
Be able to calculate cosine and inverse cosine in degree mode.
Be able to rearrange an equation to isolate an unknown.
learningOutcomes: Can you identify when the cosine rule is appropriate?
Can you calculate a missing side from two sides and their included angle?
Can you calculate an angle when all three sides are known?

name: Using R_x = Rcos(θ) for the resultant x-component
prerequisites: Be able to identify the opposite, adjacent and hypotenuse sides relative to an angle in a right-angled triangle.
Be able to use cos(theta) = adjacent / hypotenuse.
Be able to evaluate cosine in degree mode.
Be able to identify positive and negative directions on the x-axis.
learningOutcomes: Can you identify when the given angle is measured from the horizontal axis?
Can you calculate the horizontal component using R_x = R cos(theta) for that angle?
Can you assign the correct sign and unit to the horizontal component?

name: Using R_y = Rcos(θ) for the resultant y-component
prerequisites: Be able to identify the opposite, adjacent and hypotenuse sides relative to an angle in a right-angled triangle.
Be able to use cos(theta) = adjacent / hypotenuse.
Be able to evaluate cosine in degree mode.
Be able to identify positive and negative directions on the y-axis.
learningOutcomes: Can you identify when theta is measured from the vertical axis, so the vertical component is adjacent?
Can you calculate R_y = R cos(theta) when theta is measured from the vertical axis?
Can you explain why an angle measured from the horizontal instead gives R_y = R sin(theta)?
Can you assign the correct sign and unit to the vertical component?

name: Find Resultant Vector Graphically Using the Tail-to- Head Method As Well As By Calculation
prerequisites: Be able to draw an arrow to represent a given magnitude and direction.
Be able to use a ruler, protractor and drawing scale.
Be able to use Pythagoras' theorem to find a missing side of a right-angled triangle.
Be able to use tangent and inverse tangent in degree mode.
learningOutcomes: Can you place perpendicular vectors tail-to-head without changing their magnitudes or directions?
Can you draw and measure the resultant from the first tail to the final head?
Can you calculate the magnitude and direction of the resultant of perpendicular vectors?
Can you compare your calculated result with your scale drawing?

name: Determining the Magnitude of the Resultant Using Theorem of Pythagoras
prerequisites: Be able to identify the hypotenuse of a right-angled triangle.
Be able to use Pythagoras' theorem to find one side when the other two are known.
Be able to square a number and calculate a square root.
Be able to identify perpendicular directions in a diagram.
learningOutcomes: Can you identify the right-angled triangle formed by perpendicular components and their resultant?
Can you calculate R = sqrt(R_x^2 + R_y^2)?
Can you give the magnitude as a non-negative value with the correct unit?

name: A Closed Vector Diagram
prerequisites: Be able to represent magnitude and direction with an arrow.
Be able to place arrows tail-to-head.
Be able to identify a vector's starting point and ending point.
learningOutcomes: Can you recognise a closed tail-to-head vector diagram?
Can you explain why its resultant is zero?
Can you draw a vector that closes a given vector diagram?

name: Determining the Direction of the Resultant Using Simple Trigonometric Ratio
prerequisites: Be able to identify the opposite, adjacent and hypotenuse sides relative to an angle in a right-angled triangle.
Be able to use tan(theta) = opposite / adjacent.
Be able to use inverse tangent on a calculator in degree mode.
Be able to identify the four quadrants and the signs of x- and y-components.
learningOutcomes: Can you calculate a reference angle from two non-zero perpendicular components?
Can you use the component signs to place the resultant in the correct quadrant?
Can you state its direction relative to a named axis or compass direction?
Can you identify the direction directly when one component is zero?

name: Defining Normal Force
prerequisites: Be able to identify which objects are touching in a situation.
Be able to identify the surface supporting an object.
Be able to distinguish a push from a pull.
learningOutcomes: Can you describe normal force as the perpendicular contact force exerted by a surface on an object?
Can you identify the object exerting the normal force and the object receiving it?
Can you explain why normal force is not always equal to the object's weight?

name: Understanding that Normal Force Acts Perpendicular to the Surface
prerequisites: Be able to recognise a right angle.
Be able to draw a line perpendicular to a surface in a diagram.
Be able to identify the object and the surface in contact.
learningOutcomes: Can you draw the normal force perpendicular to a horizontal surface?
Can you draw the normal force perpendicular to an inclined surface?
Can you show the force pointing away from the surface on the supported object?

name: Defining Frictional Force
prerequisites: Be able to identify two surfaces that are touching.
Be able to describe the direction of relative sliding or its tendency.
Be able to represent a force with an arrow.
learningOutcomes: Can you describe friction as a contact force opposing relative sliding or its tendency?
Can you identify the surfaces between which friction acts?
Can you indicate the friction force parallel to the contact surface in a simple situation?

name: Distinguishing Between Static and Kinetic Friction Forces
prerequisites: Be able to identify the two surfaces in contact.
Be able to tell whether the surfaces slide relative to one another.
Be able to identify the direction in which sliding occurs or would occur.
learningOutcomes: Can you distinguish static friction from kinetic friction using relative sliding?
Can you identify the appropriate type of friction in a given situation?
Can you explain that static friction can vary, while its maximum value is a limit?

name: Understanding What is Meant by the Maximum Static Friction
prerequisites: Be able to distinguish sliding from no sliding at a contact surface.
Be able to compare the magnitudes of two forces.
Be able to interpret the phrase 'maximum value' as an upper limit.
learningOutcomes: Can you explain that maximum static friction is reached just before sliding begins?
Can you distinguish actual static friction from its maximum possible value?
Can you predict whether an object starts sliding when the required friction exceeds that maximum?

name: Calculating the Value of the Maximum Static Frictional Force
prerequisites: Be able to identify the normal force at a contact surface.
Be able to substitute values into a formula and multiply decimal numbers.
Be able to distinguish a force measured in newtons from a dimensionless coefficient.
Be able to distinguish a maximum limit from an actual measured value.
learningOutcomes: Can you calculate maximum static friction using f_s,max = mu_s N?
Can you give the answer in newtons and identify the meaning of each symbol?
Can you explain why actual static friction need not equal mu_s N?
Can you use a given normal force without automatically replacing it with weight?

name: Drawing a Force Diagram
prerequisites: Be able to identify the object being investigated.
Be able to identify contact interactions and gravitational attraction.
Be able to draw and label arrows to show directions.
learningOutcomes: Can you draw the object together with labelled arrows for the forces acting on it?
Can you associate each force with the interaction that causes it?
Can you distinguish a force arrow from an arrow indicating motion?

name: Drawing a Free Body Diagram
prerequisites: Be able to identify the object being investigated.
Be able to identify the forces acting on that object.
Be able to draw and label arrows in specified directions.
learningOutcomes: Can you represent the isolated object as a dot or simple point?
Can you draw one labelled arrow for each external force acting on it?
Can you leave out forces exerted by that object on other objects?
Can you avoid including both an original force and its components as additional independent forces?

name: Resolve two-dimensional forces into its parallel (x) and perpendicular (y) components
prerequisites: Be able to identify the opposite, adjacent and hypotenuse sides relative to an angle in a right-angled triangle.
Be able to use sine and cosine ratios to find a side.
Be able to evaluate sine and cosine in degree mode.
Be able to identify the chosen positive x- and y-directions.
learningOutcomes: Can you choose axes parallel and perpendicular to the relevant surface?
Can you identify which component is adjacent or opposite to the given angle?
Can you calculate the two components using the correct trigonometric ratios?
Can you give each component the correct sign and unit?

name: The resultant or net force in the x-direction is a vector sum of all the components in the x-direction
prerequisites: Be able to identify the x-component of each force in a diagram.
Be able to choose and label a positive horizontal direction.
Be able to add and subtract signed numbers.
Be able to express force values in the same unit.
learningOutcomes: Can you assign a positive or negative sign to each x-component?
Can you calculate F_net,x by adding all signed x-components?
Can you interpret the sign and zero value of the net x-force?
Can you include each force component once, without double-counting its original force?

name: The resultant or net force in the y-direction is a vector sum of all the components in the y-direction
prerequisites: Be able to identify the y-component of each force in a diagram.
Be able to choose and label a positive vertical direction.
Be able to add and subtract signed numbers.
Be able to express force values in the same unit.
learningOutcomes: Can you assign a positive or negative sign to each y-component?
Can you calculate F_net,y by adding all signed y-components?
Can you interpret the sign and zero value of the net y-force?
Can you include each force component once, without double-counting its original force?
